0x00.name: read_system_parameter
0x00.description: Read a system parameter, addressed by the command code that sets it

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Command code of the parameter to read, e.g. 0x82 for the work mode

response.format: CAN_ID | n+1 | code | param(n-1 bytes) | CRC

notes: The echoed code in byte0 is the parameter's own command code, not 0x00
The parameter is returned in the same layout used to set it, so the response DLC varies by parameter and is not fixed
A parameter that cannot be read answers DLC 4 with 0xFF 0xFF in place of the value
Manual section 5.9; added in firmware V1.0.6

0x30.name: read_encoder_carry
0x30.description: Read encoder value with carry format
notes: carry: the carry value of the encoder
value: current value of encoder (range 0~0x3FFF)
When value > 0x3FFF, carry += 1
When value < 0, carry -= 1

examples.description: Current carry|value is 0x3FF0, after one turn CCW becomes 0x13FF0

0x31.name: read_encoder_addition
0x31.description: Read encoder value in addition format
notes: After one turn CCW, the value += 0x4000
After one turn CW, the value -= 0x4000

Manual V1.0.6 is self-contradictory here: the prose summary states the opposite, but the worked example ('current value 0x3FF0, after one turn CCW the value(+0x4000) is 0x7FF0') and the sign note on 0x32 both give CCW positive. The examples are taken as authoritative.

examples.description: Current value 0x3FF0, after CCW turn becomes 0x7FF0

0x32.name: read_speed_rpm
0x32.description: Read real-time speed of motor in RPM
notes: Speed is returned in RPM (revolutions per minute)
Positive values indicate counter-clockwise (CCW) rotation
Negative values indicate clockwise (CW) rotation
Manual V1.0.6, command 0x32: 'if it run CCW, the speed > 0 (RPM); if it run CW, the speed < 0 (RPM)'

0x33.name: read_pulses_received
0x33.description: Read the number of pulses received
notes: Counts command pulses, not raw encoder counts; the screen shows the same figure as 0clk

0x34.name: read_io_ports
notes: Bit field representing status of various IO ports
Specific bit meanings depend on motor configuration

0x35.name: read_encoder_raw
0x35.description: Read the raw encoder value (addition), before calibration correction
notes: After one turn CCW, the value += 0x4000
After one turn CW, the value -= 0x4000

Manual V1.0.6 is self-contradictory here: the prose summary states the opposite, but the worked example ('current value 0x3FF0, after one turn CCW the value(+0x4000) is 0x7FF0') and the sign note on 0x32 both give CCW positive. The examples are taken as authoritative.
Same layout as 0x31, but the encoder's raw accumulator rather than the corrected one
Added in firmware V1.0.6

0x36.name: write_io_port

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Value to write to IO port

notes: Allows writing to configurable IO ports
Added in firmware V1.0.6

0x39.name: read_shaft_angle_error
0x39.description: Read the error between the commanded and the real shaft angle
notes: 0 to 51200 corresponds to 0 to 360 degrees, so one degree of error reads as 51200/360 = 142
The error is the commanded angle minus the real-time angle

0x3A.name: read_en_pin_status
0x3A.description: Read the state of the En pin

0x3B.name: read_power_on_zero_status
0x3B.description: Read the status of the go-back-to-zero-on-power-on function
notes: This is a status read, not a command to home the motor
Homing is commanded with 0x91

0x3D.name: release_protection
0x3D.description: Release motor shaft locked-rotor protection state

0x3F.name: restore_default_parameters
notes: The motor reboots afterwards and has to be recalibrated
Holding Next while powering on does the same thing

0x41.name: restart_motor
notes: Added in firmware V1.0.6
Restarts motor after error conditions

0x80.name: motor_calibration

parameters.name: reserved
parameters.description: Always 0x00; the manual shows no other value

notes: The motor must be unloaded while calibrating
Same as the Cal option on screen
Referenced as the example in the manual's CRC calculation

0x82.name: set_work_mode

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 CR_OPEN, 1 CR_CLOSE, 2 CR_vFOC, 3 SR_OPEN, 4 SR_CLOSE, 5 SR_vFOC

notes: OPEN modes cap at 400 RPM, CLOSE at 1500 RPM, vFOC at 3000 RPM
The CAN command set in Part 6 of the manual requires a serial mode (SR_OPEN, SR_CLOSE or SR_vFOC)

0x83.name: set_working_current
0x83.description: Set the working current in milliamps
notes: Maximum 3000 mA on the SERVO42D/28D/35D and 5200 mA on the SERVO57D
The value is a current in milliamps, not a percentage

0x84.name: set_subdivision
notes: The speed parameter is calibrated for 16, 32 and 64 subdivisions; other subdivisions scale from 16

0x85.name: set_en_pin_active_level
0x85.description: Set the active level of the En pin

parameters.name: enable
parameters.description: 0 active low, 1 active high, 2 active always (hold)

0x86.name: set_motor_direction
notes: Applies to the pulse interface only; in serial mode the direction is carried in each motion command

0x87.name: set_auto_screen_off
0x87.description: Turn the automatic screen blanking on or off
notes: When enabled the screen blanks after about 15 seconds and any key wakes it

0x88.name: set_stall_protection
0x88.description: Turn locked-rotor protection on or off
notes: Once triggered it is released by the Enter key, by command 0x3D, or by dropping En in pulse-interface mode

0x89.name: set_subdivision_interpolation
0x89.description: Turn subdivision interpolation on or off

0x8B.name: set_can_id
notes: 0 is the broadcast address
The new address appears in the CanID menu option

0x8C.name: set_slave_respond_active
0x8C.description: Choose whether the motor answers commands, and whether it reports completion unprompted

parameters.name: respon
parameters.description: 0 no reply at all, 1 reply to commands (default)

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: 0 no unprompted frames, 1 report completion unprompted (default)

notes: respon=0: the motor returns nothing, whatever active is set to; poll it with 0xF1 instead
respon=1, active=0: the motor acknowledges a motion command immediately with 'starting' or 'fail', and says nothing when the move ends
respon=1, active=1 (default): the immediate acknowledgement, then a second frame carrying 'complete' or 'end limit stopped' when the move ends
Same as the CanRSP menu option; revised in firmware V1.0.4 to add the active byte

0x8D.name: set_group_id
0x8D.description: Set the group address the motor also answers to
notes: A command sent to a group address moves every motor in that group
The motor does not answer a command addressed to a group, exactly as for the broadcast address
Added in firmware V1.0.1

0x8F.name: set_key_lock
0x8F.description: Lock or unlock the front-panel keys
notes: Added in firmware V1.0.3

0x90.name: set_home_parameters
0x90.description: Set the homing trigger level, direction, speed and limit behaviour

request.format: CAN_ID | 8 | 0x90 | homeTrig(uint8) | homeDir(uint8) | homeSpeed(uint16) | EndLimit(uint8) | mode(uint8) | CRC

parameters.name: homeTrig
parameters.description: Effective level of the end stop: 0 low, 1 high

parameters.name: homeDir
parameters.description: Direction of travel when homing: 0 CW, 1 CCW

parameters.name: EndLimit
parameters.description: 0 disable the endstop limit, 1 enable it

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 home against a limit switch, 1 home without one

notes: Homing is required after enabling EndLimit for the first time or changing the limit parameters
With EndLimit=1 the shaft is unlocked when homing reaches the left limit switch; set EndLimit=0 to keep it locked

0x91.name: go_home
notes: Answers 'home start' immediately, then emits a second frame with the same command byte carrying 'home success' or 'home fail'
Homing parameters are configured with 0x90

0x92.name: set_position_zero
0x92.description: Set current position to zero point
notes: Added in firmware V1.0.1
Sets current position as the zero reference point

0x94.name: set_nolimit_home_params
0x94.description: Set the return angle and current for homing without a limit switch

parameters.name: retValue
parameters.description: Reverse angle in encoder counts, big-endian; 0x4000 is a full turn, 0x2000 the default half turn

notes: Corresponds to the Hm_Mode and Hm_Ma menu options; used with 0x90 and 0x91
Added in firmware V1.0.5

0x9A.name: set_zero_mode_parameters

request.format: CAN_ID | 6 | 0x9A | mode(uint8) | enable(uint8) | speed(uint8) | dir(uint8) | CRC

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: 0 disable, 1 DirMode (return with direction), 2 NearMode (return by the smaller angle)

parameters.name: enable
parameters.description: 0 clear the zero point, 1 set it here, 2 leave it unchanged

notes: The zero-return travel covers at most 359 degrees
Added in firmware V1.0.3

0x9B.name: set_holding_current_percentage
0x9B.description: Set the holding current as a percentage of the working current

parameters.name: holdMa
parameters.description: 0x00 is 10%, rising in 10% steps to 0x08 for 90%

notes: Effective in OPEN and CLOSE modes only; vFOC ignores it
Added in firmware V1.0.4

0x9D.name: set_en_trigger_pos_error_protection
0x9D.description: Configure En-triggered single-turn zeroing and position-error protection

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: bit1 = En-triggered zeroing, bit0 = position-error protection; bits 7:2 reserved and zero

parameters.name: times
parameters.description: Length of the error statistics window, big-endian; one unit is about 15 ms

parameters.name: errors
parameters.description: Position error that triggers protection, big-endian; 28000 is a full turn out of position

notes: With En-triggered zeroing on, the motor no longer zeroes at power-on; a pulse of about 200 ms on En triggers it instead
Position-error protection and stall protection are independent; the screen shows Wrong2 for the former and Wrong for the latter
Added in firmware V1.0.6

0x9E.name: set_limit_port_remap
0x9E.description: Remap the limit inputs onto the En and Dir ports
notes: Serial control mode only; it gives the 28D/35D/42D a right-hand limit they otherwise lack
Left limit maps to the En port and right limit to the Dir port, and Com must be tied high
With remapping on, 0x34 reports IN_1 as En and IN_2 as Dir
Added in firmware V1.0.4

0xF1.name: query_motor_status
0xF1.description: Query what the motor is currently doing
notes: The way to follow a motor whose uplink frames have been switched off with 0x8C

0xF4.name: move_relative_axis
0xF4.description: Relative motion by axis, in raw encoder counts

parameters.name: relAxis
parameters.description: Signed distance in raw encoder counts, big-endian

notes: Counts are raw encoder units (16384 per motor revolution), not microsteps
Stop is encoded as this command with speed and relAxis both zero
Counter-clockwise is positive; see the errata block

0xF5.name: move_absolute_axis
0xF5.description: Absolute motion by axis, in raw encoder counts

parameters.name: absAxis
parameters.description: Signed target in raw encoder counts, big-endian

notes: Counts are raw encoder units (16384 per motor revolution), not microsteps
Supports real-time data update as of V1.0.5: a new target may be sent while a move is in progress, which re-plans rather than queueing
Re-targeting mid-move makes the motor emit a 'run fail' frame for the superseded move, carrying the same command byte as the acknowledgement of the new one
Stop is encoded as this command with speed and absAxis both zero
Bug fixed in V1.0.4

0xF6.name: run_speed_mode
0xF6.description: Run continuously at a set speed and acceleration

parameters.name: dir_speed_high
parameters.description: bit7 = direction (0 CCW, 1 CW), bits 3:0 = speed high nibble

notes: Speed 0 is the stop command: acc non-zero decelerates, acc 0 stops immediately
Manual worked example: 01 F6 01 40 02 3A runs forward at acc=2, speed=320 RPM; 01 F6 81 40 02 BA runs in reverse at the same speed
The uplink frame can be switched off with 0x8C or the CanRSP menu option

0xF7.name: emergency_stop
notes: Added in firmware V1.0.4
Immediately stops motor movement

0xFD.name: move_relative_pulses
0xFD.description: Relative motion by pulses, in command microsteps

request.format: CAN_ID | 8 | 0xFD | dir+speed_high(uint8) | speed_low(uint8) | acc(uint8) | pulses(uint24) | CRC

parameters.name: dir_speed_high
parameters.description: bit7 = direction (0 CCW, 1 CW), bits 3:0 = speed high nibble

parameters.name: pulses
parameters.description: Magnitude in command microsteps, big-endian; sign is in dir

notes: Pulses are command microsteps (base steps x MSTEP), not raw encoder counts
Direction is a flag, not the sign of the pulse count

0xFE.name: move_absolute_pulses
0xFE.description: Absolute motion by pulses, in command microsteps

parameters.name: absPulses
parameters.description: Signed target in command microsteps, big-endian

notes: Pulses are command microsteps (base steps x MSTEP), not raw encoder counts
Stop is encoded as this command with speed and absPulses both zero

0xFF.name: save_clean_speed_mode_params
0xFF.description: Save or clear the speed-mode parameters used at power-on
notes: With parameters saved, the motor turns at the saved constant speed as soon as it is powered on
0xC8 and 0xCA are values of this command's argument, not command codes of their own

categories.status: Commands for reading motor status, encoder values, and system state
categories.motion: Commands for controlling motor movement and positioning
categories.control: Commands for motor control operations (enable, disable, protection)
categories.configuration: Commands for motor setup, calibration, and parameter setting

errata.sign_convention: Counter-clockwise is positive for both encoder accumulation (0x31/0x35) and reported speed (0x32). The prose summaries above the 0x31 and 0x35 worked examples in manual V1.0.6 state the reverse; they are wrong, as shown by the examples immediately below them and by the 0x32 note.
errata.command_naming: Commands 0xF4 and 0xF5 act on the axis (raw encoder counts); 0xFD and 0xFE act on pulses (command microsteps). Earlier revisions of this fixture named 0xF4/0xF5 as pulse commands and gave them a pulses(int32)|speed(uint16) layout, which matches no command in the manual. It also mapped 0x3B to go_home; 0x3B reads the power-on zero status and 0x91 commands homing.
errata.dlc_cells_contradict_byte_maps: Three commands print a DLC that disagrees with the byte map beside it. 0x39's response is shown as DLC 4 over a map of code|error(int32)|CRC, which is 6. 0x94's request is shown as DLC 6 over a map of code|retValue(uint32)|ma(uint16)|CRC, which is 8. 0x9A's request is shown as DLC 5 over a map of code|mode|enable|speed|dir|CRC, which is 6. The byte maps are transcribed here; each is internally consistent with its field widths, and the DLC cells are not.
errata.calibration_frame_length: 0x80's request is DLC 3 and carries a 0x00 data byte: the manual shows '01 3 80 00 CRC(81)', and the printed CRC confirms it, (0x01 + 0x80 + 0x00) & 0xFF = 0x81. Earlier revisions of this transcription recorded DLC 2 with no arguments.
errata.printed_crc_typos: Some worked examples print a CRC that does not follow from the frame. 0x34's downlink is given as '01 34 CRC(3B)' where (0x01 + 0x34) & 0xFF = 0x35; 0x3A's 'CRC(3B)' on the following page is correct, which is the likely source of the slip. The algorithm in Part 4 governs.
errata.speed_mode_stop: 0xF6 is documented twice, once to run and once to stop, with the same frame layout: a stop is a run at speed 0. The two share a command code and differ only in their status codes, so they are one entry here.
errata.raw_encoder_response_width: 0x35's response was transcribed here as DLC 4 carrying raw_data(uint16). The manual gives DLC 8 carrying value(int48), the same layout as 0x31, and the entry's own notes - a value that moves by 0x4000 per revolution - only make sense for an accumulator. Nothing checked it: 0x35 was absent from the read commands the response-DLC test drives.

deliberately_absent.0xC8: Not a command. 0xC8 is the 'save' value of command 0xFF's state byte; constants.py exposes it as CMD_SAVE_SPEED_PARAMS.
deliberately_absent.0xCA: Not a command. 0xCA is the 'clean' value of command 0xFF's state byte; constants.py exposes it as CMD_CLEAN_SPEED_PARAMS.
